chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tawil, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'from Ishaq ibn al-Qasim' (note: variant reading), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding zakat, he said: 'What the Banu Umayya have taken from you, consider it [as sufficient], and do not give them anything as long as you are able, for wealth cannot be purified twice in the same manner.'
ai.seo_question: Do I need to pay zakat again if I already paid it to the Umayyad rulers?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declared that the wealth seized by the Umayyad caliphs counts as valid zakat, establishing the principle that the same asset is not purified twice. This ruling, recorded in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, highlights the pragmatic Shia approach to fiscal legitimacy under non-Shia rulers, ensuring believers are not burdened by double taxation while maintaining the spiritual integrity of their wealth.
